items.title: Three Kinds of Purity, and Why the Three Jewels Are Called Supreme

items.zh: 云何淨？謂三清淨性。一、自體清淨性，二、境界清淨性，三、分位清淨性。云何妙？謂佛法僧寶名最微妙。墮最第一施設中故。
items.en: What is purity? Three kinds of the nature of purity. First, the nature of intrinsic purity; second, the nature of the purity of [its] object; third, the nature of purity by stage. What is excellence? The jewels of the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha are called the most subtle and excellent, because they fall within the very first rank of what can be designated [as excellent].

items.title: Tranquility, and the Five Aspects Under Which Anything Has a "Nature"

items.zh: 云何寂靜？謂從善法欲，乃至一切菩提分法，及所得果，皆名寂靜。云何性？謂諸法體相。若自相、若共相、若假立相、若因相、若果相等。
items.en: What is tranquility? From the wholesome aspiration [for nirvāṇa] up through all the factors of enlightenment, together with the fruits thereby attained — all of this is called tranquility. What is nature? The intrinsic character of phenomena: whether their own particular characteristic, their characteristic held in common [with other phenomena], their provisionally posited characteristic, their characteristic as cause, or their characteristic as fruit, and so forth.

items.title: The Four Principles of Reasoning, Provisional Designation, and the Six Kinds of Direct Realisation — the First Verse Closes

items.zh: 云何道理？謂諸緣起及四道理。云何假施設？謂於唯法假立補特伽羅，及於唯相假立諸法。云何現觀？謂六現觀。如有尋有伺地已說。
items.en: What is principle? Dependent origination, and the four principles [of reasoning]. What is provisional designation? Positing a person upon what is merely phenomena, and positing all phenomena upon what is merely characteristic-marks. What is direct realisation? The six kinds of direct realisation, as already explained in the Ground With Applied and Sustained Thought.

items.title: The Second Verse Opens: The Five Aggregates Renamed by Their Defining Function

items.zh: 復次，嗢拕南曰：方所、位、分別、作、執持、增、減、冥、言、所覺、上、遠離、轉、藏護。云何方所？謂色蘊。云何位？謂受蘊。云何分別？謂想蘊。云何作？謂行蘊。云何執持？謂識蘊。
items.en: Furthermore, the summarising verse says: "Location, stage, discrimination; making, holding-fast, increase and decrease; obscurity, speech, what is understood; the higher, seclusion, turning, and clinging-and-guarding." What is location? The aggregate of form. What is stage? The aggregate of feeling. What is discrimination? The aggregate of perception. What is making? The aggregate of formations. What is holding-fast? The aggregate of consciousness.

items.title: Increase and Decrease, the Darkness of Ignorance and Doubt, Speech, and What Is Understood

items.zh: 云何增？謂有二種。一、煩惱增，二、業增。如增有二種，當知減、亦爾。云何冥？謂無明及疑。云何言？謂諸如來十二分教、說名為言。云何所覺？謂彼彼言音所說之義、名為所覺。
items.en: What is increase? There are two kinds: the increase of affliction, and the increase of karma. As increase has two kinds, know that decrease is likewise so. What is darkness? Ignorance and doubt. What is speech? The Tathāgata's twelve divisions of teaching are called speech. What is that which is understood? The meaning spoken through this or that utterance is called that which is understood.

items.title: The Higher Fruits, Five Kinds of Seclusion, Transmigration, and Clinging to the Three Times — the Second Verse Closes

items.zh: 云何上？謂四沙門果。云何遠離？謂五種遠離。一、惡行遠離，二、欲遠離，三、資具遠離，四、憒鬧遠離，五、煩惱遠離。云何轉？謂三界、五趣。云何藏護？謂追戀過去，希慕未來，耽著現在。
items.en: What is the higher? The four fruits of the ascetic path. What is seclusion? Five kinds of seclusion: first, seclusion from wrongdoing; second, seclusion from desire; third, seclusion from [attachment to] requisites; fourth, seclusion from clamour; fifth, seclusion from affliction. What is turning? The three realms and the five destinies. What is clinging-and-guarding? Longing after the past, yearning for the future, and being engrossed in the present.

items.title: The Third Verse Opens: Six Logical Forms for Clarifying Doctrine Through Question and Answer

items.zh: 復次，嗢拕南曰：思擇、與現行、睡眠、及相屬、諸相攝、相應、說、任持、次第。云何思擇？謂一行、順前句、順後句、四句、無事句。
items.en: Furthermore, the summarising verse says: "Investigation and manifestation; sleep, and mutual relation; comprehension, correspondence; speaking, sustaining, and sequence." What is investigation? A single series, the forward-conforming statement, the backward-conforming statement, the four-cornered statement, and the groundless statement.

items.title: Investigation Continues: Seventy-One Paired Categories Spanning the Entire Field of Phenomena

items.zh: 復有有色法、無色法、有見法、無見法，有對法、無對法、有漏法、無漏法、有為法、無為法，有諍法、無諍法、有味著法、無味著法、依耽嗜法、依出離法、世間法、出世間法、有繫屬法、無繫屬法、內法、外法、麁法、細法、劣法、勝法、遠法、近法、有所緣法、無所緣法、相應法、不相應法、有行法、無行法、有依法、無依法、因法、非因法、果法、非果法、異熟法、非異熟法、有因法、非有因法、有果法、非有果法、有異熟法、非有異熟法、有執受法、無執受法、大種造法、非大種造法、同分法、彼同分法、有上法、無上法、又有過去法、未來法、現在法、善法、不善法、無記法、欲繫法、色繫法、無色繫法、學法、無學法、非學非無學法、見所斷法、修所斷法、無斷法。
items.en: There are also: phenomena with form, and without form; visible, and invisible; resistant, and non-resistant; with outflow, and without outflow; conditioned, and unconditioned; contentious, and non-contentious; with attachment-savour, and without attachment-savour; dependent on indulgence, and dependent on renunciation; worldly, and world-transcending; bound [to the three realms], and unbound; internal, and external; coarse, and subtle; inferior, and superior; distant, and near; with an object, and without an object; conjoined, and unconjoined; with activity, and without activity; with support, and without support; causal, and non-causal; resultant, and non-resultant; ripened, and unripened; with a cause, and without a cause; with a fruit, and without a fruit; with ripening, and without ripening; appropriated, and unappropriated; made of the great elements, and not made of the great elements; of shared category, and of that same category [without the corresponding consciousness]; with something higher, and unsurpassed; and further: past, future, and present; wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate; bound to the desire realm, the form realm, and the formless realm; belonging to the trainee, the adept beyond training, and neither; to be severed by the path of seeing, to be severed by the path of cultivation, and not to be severed at all.

items.title: The Four Conditions, and the Four Reliances — "Investigation" Concludes

items.zh: 又有四緣。謂因緣、等無間緣、所緣緣、增上緣。又有四依。一、法是依，非補特伽羅；二、義是依、非文；三、了義經是依，非不了義；四、智是依，非識。又有四無量法、四念住法、四正斷法、四神足法、五根法、五力法、七覺支法、八支聖道法、四行跡法、四法跡法、奢摩他法、毘鉢舍那法、增上戒法、增上心法、增上慧法、解脫法、勝處法、遍處法。如是等法無量無邊，應當思擇。
items.en: There are also four conditions: the causal condition, the condition of equal and uninterrupted succession, the condition of the object, and the dominant condition. There are also four reliances: first, one relies on the Dharma, not on the person; second, one relies on the meaning, not on the letter; third, one relies on the definitive teaching, not on the provisional teaching; fourth, one relies on wisdom, not on [ordinary] consciousness. Phenomena such as these are boundless and beyond measure, and should be thoroughly investigated.

items.title: Manifest Affliction, Dormant Affliction, and Three Kinds of Mutual Relation

items.zh: 云何現行？謂諸煩惱纏。云何睡眠？謂諸煩惱隨眠。云何相屬？謂內六處於一身中，當知展轉互相繫屬。又若此法能引彼法，當知此彼互相繫屬。又諸根境，當知能取、所取互相繫屬。
items.en: What is manifestation? The afflictions that bind [the mind]. What is dormancy? The afflictions lying latent [as seeds]. What is mutual relation? The six inner sense-bases within a single body should be known to be mutually related to one another, turn by turn. Furthermore, if one phenomenon is able to draw forth another, know that the two are mutually related. Furthermore, the faculties and their objects should be known to be mutually related as grasper and grasped.

items.title: Sixteen Ways to Comprehend the Aggregates, Elements, and Sense-Fields

items.zh: 云何攝？謂十六種攝。一、界攝，二、相攝，三、種類攝，四、分位攝，五、不相離攝，六、時攝，七、方攝，八、一分攝，九、具分攝，十、勝義攝，十一、蘊攝，十二、界攝，十三、處攝，十四、緣起攝，十五、處非處攝，十六、根攝。
items.en: What is comprehension? Sixteen kinds of comprehension. First, comprehension by [seed-]element; second, comprehension by characteristic; third, comprehension by category; fourth, comprehension by stage; fifth, comprehension by inseparability; sixth, comprehension by time; seventh, comprehension by place; eighth, comprehension by a single part; ninth, comprehension in full; tenth, comprehension by ultimate meaning; eleventh, comprehension by the aggregates; twelfth, comprehension by the elements; thirteenth, comprehension by the sense-fields; fourteenth, comprehension by dependent origination; fifteenth, comprehension by what is and is not the case; sixteenth, comprehension by the faculties.

blocks.text: Today continues the verse of key terms from the Stage Attained Through Hearing. It reads like a dictionary entry for each term, which it is: these are the words a hearer must understand before reflection can begin. The commentary picks out the entries our teachers explain most vividly.

Purity may be by nature, by stage, or by completeness. Master Cháng Bǎi on purity by stage: stream-entry is less pure than once-return, and so on to arhatship. The Three Jewels are called supreme because they are rare and of great value.

"Nature" (性) is the character of phenomena. Venerable Miào Jìng distinguishes it from "mark" (相): "going from outside in is called nature; from inside out can be called mark." We see the mark; we infer the nature.
Four principles of reasoning (四種道理): dependence, efficacy, proof, and the nature of things. These recur throughout Yogācāra as the standards by which any teaching is examined.

**Provisional designation** (假施設) posits a person on mere phenomena. Venerable Miào Jìng's example: Empress Wu coined a new character for her own name, 曌, sun and moon over the sky. Names are made; Buddhism denies not that names work, but that they name a real essence (Day 44).

The second verse renames the aggregates by function: form is **location**, feeling is **stage**, perception is **discrimination**, formations are **making**, and consciousness is **holding-fast** (執持). Master Cháng Bǎi on the last: "Because the ālaya holds them, beings' bodies endure; if it didn't hold the body, it would be like a corpse." The ālayavijñāna appears here as the meaning of the fifth aggregate.

"Darkness" is ignorance and doubt. "Speech" is the Tathāgata's twelve divisions of teaching. Among five kinds of seclusion is seclusion from clamour; Venerable Miào Jìng: "If their thoughts don't agree, even two people are clamour." "Clinging-and-guarding" (藏護) is longing for past, future, and present. Master Cháng Bǎi: 藏 is attachment to one's own life; 護 is attachment to others as "mine".

The third verse opens with "investigation" (思擇), in five logical forms: a single series, forward-conforming, backward-conforming, four-cornered, and groundless. Venerable Miào Jìng on the last: the fourth corner, "neither form nor non-form", leaves nothing to stand on; that is the groundless statement. Seventy-one paired categories follow, spanning the whole field of phenomena: a full Abhidharma in miniature.

"Manifestation" is afflictions that bind the mind now; "dormancy" is the latent afflictions (Day 7, Day 54). Things are mutually related when one draws forth another. Venerable Miào Jìng's example: the six sense-bases draw forth the six consciousnesses.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain "purity by stage" among the three purities?
options: stream-entry is less pure than once-return, and so on up to arhatship — purity differing by stage
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "Stream-entry isn't as pure as once-return, once-return not as pure as non-return, non-return not as pure as arhatship — that's purity by stage." Venerable Miào Jìng: purity of object is the verbal Dharma — sūtra, vinaya, treatise.

quiz.q: The text says "nature" is phenomena's character. How does Venerable Miào Jìng distinguish 性 and 相?
options: moving from outer to inner is nature; from inner to outer is mark
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "Going from outside in is called nature; from inside out can be called mark." Master Cháng Bǎi, citing the *Mahāprajñāpāramitā-śāstra*: nature and mark aren't different. The text lists own, common, posited, causal, and resultant characteristics.

quiz.q: Provisional designation posits a person on mere phenomena. What example does Venerable Miào Jìng use?
options: Empress Wu coining the character 曌 (sun and moon over sky) — names are constructed
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "She invented a character — 明 for sun and moon, with 空 beneath — called 曌." Buddhism denies a substantial self but accepts a nominal self. Master Cháng Bǎi: all talk of self and dharmas is conventional designation.

quiz.q: The second verse renames the aggregates by function. Which mapping is correct?
options: location — form; stage — feeling; discrimination — perception; making — formations; holding-fast — consciousness
quiz.why: "What is location? The aggregate of form. What is stage? The aggregate of feeling. What is discrimination? The aggregate of perception. What is making? The aggregate of formations. What is holding-fast? The aggregate of consciousness." Master Cháng Bǎi: form is "location" because direction depends on it and it occupies space.

quiz.q: Consciousness is "holding-fast." What happens if the ālaya doesn't hold the body, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: it would be like a corpse, soon rotting — beings' bodies last because the ālaya holds them
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "Because the ālaya holds them, beings' bodies endure; if it didn't hold the body, it would be like a corpse, soon decaying." Venerable Miào Jìng: one's fate is self-made, from the seeds the ālaya holds.

quiz.q: Among five kinds of seclusion is seclusion from clamour. What does Venerable Miào Jìng say counts as clamour?
options: if minds don't agree, even two people are clamour
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "If their thoughts don't agree, even two people are clamour — it doesn't have to be hundreds or thousands." The text: seclusion from wrongdoing, desire, requisites, clamour, affliction. Master Cháng Bǎi: differing aims make two people noisy.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, what are "manifestation" and "dormancy"?
options: manifestation is afflictions that bind; dormancy is latent afflictions
quiz.why: "What is manifestation? The afflictions that bind the mind. What is dormancy? The afflictions lying latent." Master Cháng Bǎi: "Afflictions wrap around the mind like a rope, making it unfree."
